name: Saint Lucia
prevalence_note: Government of Saint Lucia, RSLPF & ECCB 2025-2026: fake Saint Lucia Postal Service parcel/customs smishing links, bank debit-card/OTP vishing and soft-spoken 'guess who' relative calls, and unlicensed crypto pyramid schemes (e.g. Creators Alliance) dominate.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-758 within NANP and the ECCU; scammers send smishing links from `.top` domains and spoof local +1-758 / overseas +1 numbers.

scams.name: Fake Saint Lucia Postal Service / Customs Parcel Hold Scam
scams.name_en: Fraudulent Saint Lucia Postal Service message or call claiming an undeliverable parcel needs fee/data
scams.signals_en: SMS, email, or call claiming a parcel at the Saint Lucia Postal Service or customs cannot be delivered without clicking a lookalike link (such as `.top` domains) and entering card details.
scams.legit_en: The Government of Saint Lucia confirms the Postal Service never texts third-party links demanding personal or card data to release mail.
bait_tactics: Say you work right near the Castries General Post Office and will walk over with your ID slip at lunch.
Ask what country the parcel was mailed from before touching any link.
Pretend your phone has no data plan to open web links.

scams.name: Bank Debit-Card OTP Vishing & Low-Voice Impersonation Call
scams.name_en: RSLPF & ECCB-warned bank OTP vishing or soft-spoken caller tricking victim into naming a contact
scams.signals_en: Caller either poses as bank security asking for debit-card/OTP codes, or speaks softly waiting for the victim to guess a friend/business owner's name and then asks for urgent cash or phone credit.
scams.legit_en: RSLPF warns never to volunteer names to vague callers or send cash/codes without calling the person's known official number.
bait_tactics: Refuse to guess a name—ask the caller to state their full company role clearly first.
Tell a supposed bank caller you will verify at your Castries or Vieux Fort branch in person.
Say you have zero credit or cash on hand and need to ring them back on their office landline.

scams.name: Unlicensed Crypto Pyramid & Fake Lottery Fee Scam
scams.name_en: ECCB-warned unlicensed virtual-asset recruitment scheme or advance-fee prize call
scams.signals_en: Solicits deposits into unlicensed crypto/pyramid schemes promising rapid returns for recruiting friends, or demands upfront fees to release lottery winnings.
scams.legit_en: Participating in pyramid selling is an offence in Saint Lucia, and legitimate investments must be licensed by the ECSRC/FSRA.
bait_tactics: Ask for their ECSRC or Saint Lucia FSRA virtual-asset licence status before discussing any deposit.
For a prize call, ask why fees cannot be subtracted directly from the winnings.
Say you need your accountant to review the written prospectus first.
